name: Coldpatch Elder Coat & Walk Set
description: A full-length greatcoat in what was once a deep charcoal wool blend, now faded to a complex mix of grays and near-browns from years of acid rain, hand-washing, and sun exposure in the Shelf's filtered, dirty light. The coat falls to mid-calf and was clearly once a higher-tier garment — the construction quality beneath the damage is visible in the structured shoulders, the deep lapels, and the deliberate drape. It has been repaired so extensively that the repairs have become its primary visual identity: the left shoulder sports a large patch in rubberized olive canvas, its edges sealed with silver-gray self-repair tape folded into a clean border; the right sleeve carries three sequential patch repairs in progressively darker fabrics — charcoal, then near-black, then a strip of industrial gray rubber — recording years of acid-sleeve damage. The lining is entirely replaced, now a salvaged thermal blanket material in reflective silver, visible at the hem and collar as a glinting inner layer. The coat is belted with a wide leather strap that has been broken and re-stitched twice, the repair points marked by darker color where the leather was wetted and recured. Beneath the coat, a heavyweight turtleneck in faded ash marled knit sits close to the body, its ribbing loose at the collar from stretching but intact everywhere else. Wide-leg trousers in washed near-black canvas carry side-seam pockets and a reinforced seat. Footwear is a tall boot, resoled so many times the sole is now nearly an inch thick with layered rubber, the upper a patchwork of original leather and replacement panels in synthetic suede, the whole thing treated with a heavy waterproofing compound that gives it a waxy, uneven finish. A wide-brim hat in felted gray, its crown creased and its brim slightly warped but functional, completes the silhouette. The hat carries a single ornament: a small, carefully-polished piece of chrome scrap — possibly from a salvaged aug-component — pinned to the band.
functionality: Full-length acid-rain protection from rubberized patches and thermal blanket lining; reflective interior lining for passive heat retention; resoled boots for maximum sole durability on rough terrain; wide-brim hat for acid-rain facial protection; chrome ornament is a functional pin repurposed as decoration; large coat pockets carry significant storage
what_it_says: Age. History. Survival across multiple Shelf seasons. This coat is an archive — each patch is a date, an incident, a cost survived. The original quality of the coat beneath the repairs suggests the wearer either came down from a higher tier or inherited something that outlasted its original context. The polished chrome ornament is the detail that matters: in a rig built entirely from necessity, one thing has been kept clean and bright. That's a statement about what the wearer values, and it isn't survival — it's dignity.
worn_by: long-term residents who have survived multiple acid seasons
people who came down from Tier 2 or 3 and never went back
informal Shelf historians and keepers of local memory
manufacturer: Base coat is an unidentified pre-existing garment, likely Tier 3 manufacture, date unknown; all modifications self-made; boots are multi-source resoled originals
price_range: Φ 30–60 for the full set; the coat alone may be worth Φ 40–80 to the right collector
story_hooks: The chrome ornament on the hat band is identifiable to anyone who knows aug-tech: it's a fragment of a specific neural port housing from a model discontinued fifteen years ago — the same model involved in a mass-recall scandal that killed people in the Shelf. The wearer knows exactly what it is.
Someone from Tier 3 recognizes the base coat — it was a specific garment from a specific time, and seeing it on a Shelf elder raises questions about who this person was before, and what they know.

The coat's inner lining — the salvaged thermal blanket — is stamped with a Lazarus Emergency Response batch number from a disaster relief distribution that officially covered a different district entirely. The wearer received it from someone. That someone may still be alive.
